Original JR definition, arXiv:1407.8269v1, p. 2, Definition 1
correctness.rationale: Failure of standard JR is exactly the existence of an outside candidate approved by at least r=ceil(n/k) unrepresented voters: such voters themselves form a violating group, and any violating group's common candidate must be outside the committee. The unrepresented set is determined by elected columns alone; its size U is Bin(n,q_W). Given that set, independent outside columns give Bin(U,p_c) counts, so the conditional no-violation probability is the specified product of lower tails, depending only on U. This gives the exact mixture, including q_W=0 or 1, endpoint probabilities, U=0 and the empty product at m=k. For a swap of a lower-probability winner with a higher-probability outsider, couple by common uniforms, aligning the old and new winner columns and aligning the two outside columns. The newly unrepresented voter set is contained in the old one, and each outside approval set is contained in its old counterpart or unchanged. Thus success cannot decrease, proving the finite-n maximizer, including ties, without any independence assumption on the unconditional violation counts. Rational evaluation is polynomial in numerical n, m and rational bit lengths: the supplied binomial-sum count is O(mn²) arithmetic operations and every full-mixture probability admits common denominator ∏_c d_c^n for probability denominators d_c. This is not a polynomial-time claim in log n for a succinct input with output written in full. For an outsider to a top-k committee, the per-voter violation probability is a=p_c q_W≤p_c(1−p_c)^k≤a_k<1/k. Chernoff at 1/k and the union bound give the stated uniform finite-n bound. At equal probabilities 1/(k+1) one outsider attains a_k, and the single mass at ceil(n/k) has logarithmic rate D(1/k||a_k) by Stirling for k>1. When k=1 the tail is exactly 4^(−n); the lower bound uses an outsider, so requires m>k. Squeezing for fixed m>k proves the limit after the supremum. Independently, the example's failure numerator is 6·31²+4·31+1=5891 over 32⁴, as stated.
residual_risks: The finite exact examples and numerical rates are corroborative, not a proof of the general optimizer or exponent. The exponent and optimum concern a committee fixed from parameters before sampling, not approval-score winners chosen after the profile is drawn.

evidence: The 3VA counting hardness result uses voter-varying outsider columns. Theorem 9 gives a product over outsider complements when elected approvals are deterministic and remaining uncertainty is 3VA; the unrepresented set is then fixed. Theorem 10 is the special threshold-one case k=n. These results do not give the random-U binomial mixture for stochastic winners across all n,k.

Xia covers voter-homogeneous independent approvals with heterogeneous candidate parameters and proves exponential success of all top-probability committees for EJR+ for fixed interior p. The stated theorem does not maximize exact ordinary-JR success at each finite n.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The frozen product conditioned on the unrepresented set extends the known deterministic-set case by averaging an exact random-size law. General hardness and an asymptotic stronger axiom do not subsume this tractability and exact optimizer.

evidence: Elkind et al. already identify the common-p per-outsider count with a Bernoulli sum, use the union bound, and maximize p(1−p)^k at p=1/(k+1). Xia computes the heterogeneous witness probability as p_c times the lower tail of a sum of committee approval indicators; for ℓ=1 this is exactly p_c q_W. Combining those ingredients with binomial lower and upper tail estimates is very close to the displayed sharp exponent.

Neither single-witness bound nor prior conditional product with fixed unrepresented set compares finite-n intersections across different committees with stochastic elected approvals. The finite result additionally uses voter-homogeneity to collapse the random set to its size and a simultaneous monotone exchange (or coupling) of the winning and excluded columns.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the shared per-outsider theory and the easy rate upgrade. The exact common-random-size mixture and optimizer are the materially distinct part, not an inference from qualitative high-probability JR or EJR+ success.

evidence: Aziz et al.'s original Definition 1 is the same JR axiom and uses the ceiling cutoff. The probability here is an ex-ante fixed-committee probability, not a success rate of an observed-profile voting rule.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The witness event is known and the ℓ=1 mapping is exact. What needs comparison is the probability of the intersection of all no-violation events and its finite-time optimizer, not the axiom under a new name.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct contribution is the exact conditional-size formula with all-finite-n top-k optimality in the homogeneous-by-voter heterogeneous-by-candidate class, together with the explicit uniform limiting rate. The existing JR definition, conditionally independent outsider calculation for deterministic elected columns, common-p maximization, and heterogeneous top-k exponential guarantees are credited below. The sharp exponent is especially close to a synthesis of prior bounds and textbook binomial tails; it is not treated as a wholly new probabilistic method or the sole basis for acceptance. No inspected result covers the exact finite-n mixture and selection theorem together.
residual_risks: Bounded literature and indexed comparisons do not certify priority. One related same-date catalogue record was not available in full. A routine large-deviation upgrade of the existing single-witness machinery accounts for much of the rate argument.

Aziz et al., JR-Probability and MaxJR; Elkind et al., Theorem 1; Xia, Theorem 17
value.rationale: Exact JR probability and MaxJR are naturally motivated by the general uncertain-voting problems. The result isolates a tractable nontrivial homogeneous-by-voter class and gives a one-dimensional exact calculation and a deterministic sorting rule that is optimal already at finite sizes, without treating positively correlated witness counts as independent unconditionally. The sharp worst-case rate quantifies, rather than replaces, this finite-n guarantee.
residual_risks: Restricted to independent candidate-voter Bernoulli approvals with homogeneity by voter. No stronger approved-representation axiom, observed-profile rule, or growing-candidate worst-case law is asserted.
